name: Palma
title: Ship Thickness Measurement in Palma | UTM for Ferries & Yachts
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Palma de Mallorca for ferries, cruise ships and large yachts: hull gauging, pre-docking readings and renewal survey UTM.
h1: Palma de Mallorca Hull Gauging: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ferries, Cruise Ships and Superyachts
intro: Palma is the main gateway of the Balearic Islands: a ferry hub for the Spanish mainland, a stop on most western Mediterranean cruise itineraries and the busiest superyacht refit centre in the region. Ships here run on island timetables, and a docking is usually fitted into a quiet winter gap. Atlantis NDT sends an ultrasonic gauging team out from India to the vessel, working to the refit plan, the owner's brief and the attending surveyor's format.

highlights.h: Winter refit window for island ferries
highlights.p: Ro-pax ships serving the Balearic routes thin out their schedules after the summer peak, and the off-season is when docking and renewal survey gauging gets booked. Readings taken early set the steel scope before the yard is committed.

highlights.h: Large yachts and workboats under one plan
highlights.p: Palma refits yachts above commercial-ship size as well as merchant tonnage. Where a yacht is classed, hull, tank and shell readings follow the same ultrasonic method and the same report layout as any ship.

highlights.h: Cruise turnaround days in a compact port
highlights.p: Cruise ships alongside for a day let scrubber wash-water lines, sea-water piping and technical void spaces be gauged while passengers are ashore and engine-room crews have time to give access.

port.h: The Port of Palma: island ferries, cruise ships and a yacht-refit coast
p: The Port of Palma lies along the northern shore of the Bay of Palma on the south-west coast of Mallorca, and is run by the Autoritat Portuària de Balears, which also administers the other main Balearic ports. The harbour is a long string of quays stretching along the bay front, with ferry berths close to the city, cruise berths at the outer piers and a commercial and cargo area further towards the western side. Almost everything that reaches the islands by sea in volume passes through here, which gives the port a steady base of vehicle ferries, ro-ro cargo ships and supply vessels all year round.

Passenger traffic defines the port. Fast and conventional ro-pax ferries link Palma with Barcelona, Valencia, Ibiza and Menorca, and the summer timetable is far busier than the winter one. Cruise ships on western Mediterranean loops call in large numbers from spring to late autumn, and some lines use Palma as a turnaround port, which means ships come back to the same berth on a fixed weekly pattern. Alongside this sits a large yacht and superyacht community, with refit yards, marinas and brokers concentrated around the bay. Bunker barges, tugs, pilot boats and tourist craft complete a harbour where merchant and leisure shipping share the same water.

For thickness gauging the seasonal rhythm matters more than anything else. In July a ferry cannot be spared, while in January the same ship may be idle for days. That makes winter the natural window for renewal and intermediate surveys, and it explains why enquiries in Palma often arrive in the autumn, once the operator has decided which ships will dock. The bay is sheltered from most of the prevailing weather, though a southerly swell can make anchorage work and launch boarding awkward, and the northerly tramontana is felt on the quays. Large cruise ships and big ferries take most of the berthing space in summer, so any plan that needs a quay for several days is best agreed with the port well before the season starts.

facilities.h: Quays, repair berths and refit yards around the Bay of Palma
p: Structured gauging in Palma happens either at a repair quay, where a ship lies afloat while spaces are cleaned and opened, or at one of the yards that handle larger yachts and workboats on slipways and hoists. Ferries and commercial ships generally take their major dockings at yards on the mainland, so in Palma the common job is an afloat survey: ballast tanks, void spaces, vehicle deck plating, ramps and stern doors measured ahead of the mainland docking, giving the yard a steel list to plan against before the ship arrives.

Cruise ships and ferries on fixed rotations can be gauged in stages. A cruise ship returning every week gives a technician access to the same scrubber and sea-water piping on successive turnaround days, and the readings are compiled into one report for the superintendent. Yacht work follows the refit schedule of the yard, with the team arriving once the hull has been stripped back and the tanks are opened. Ships at anchor in the bay are reached by launch arranged through the agent, which is the usual route for pre-purchase and on-hire condition gauging; because a southerly swell can stop boarding, the plan needs a spare day. All equipment travels with the technicians, so no shore gauge or staging is requested from the port.
list: Ferry berths along the city waterfront: vehicle deck, ramp, stern door and ballast tank gauging between sailings during the winter timetable
Cruise berths at the outer piers: scrubber wash-water, overboard and sea-water piping gauged on turnaround days, repeated across visits where the ship returns weekly
Repair quays in the commercial harbour: afloat gauging of tanks and voids opened for yard work, ahead of or after a docking elsewhere
Refit yards for large yachts and workboats: hull, tank and shell gauging planned around stripping, blasting and recoating
Anchorage in the Bay of Palma: pre-purchase and charter on-hire or off-hire condition gauging by launch, with a margin for swell

context.h: Regulatory picture for ships using Palma
p: Spain is a Paris MoU state, and port state control on merchant ships calling at Palma is carried out by marine inspectors working for the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante through the local Capitanía Marítima. Ro-pax ferries and passenger ships are examined with particular care, and a record of recent thickness readings on vehicle decks, ramps and ballast spaces helps an operator show that wastage is understood and monitored. The Balearic Islands are inside the Mediterranean SOx Emission Control Area, which is why scrubber-fitted cruise ships and ferries keep their systems running at Palma and why the wash-water pipework is a recurring gauging target.

Island shipping also feels the effect of EU carbon rules. Shipping has been covered by the EU Emissions Trading System since 2024, and FuelEU Maritime has applied from 2025, so ferry operators weigh the future of older tonnage against newer replacements. A sale, a charter extension or a decision to keep a ship in service is easier when the steel condition is documented. Regular readings also support the EU Ship Recycling Regulation's requirement for an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, since an owner who knows the structure's condition plans end-of-life decisions with better information. Large yachts above commercial thresholds may fall under different rules from merchant ships, so we confirm with the owner which framework the readings serve.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Palma
jobs.p: Palma enquiries cluster around the end of the summer season, when operators decide which ships to dock and owners of yachts book winter refits. Most work is planned weeks ahead, with scope, spaces and report format agreed before the team travels. Where a ship will be docked elsewhere, we treat Palma as the place to collect data so that the yard has a realistic steel estimate in hand. Typical requests include:
list: Pre-docking gauging of vehicle decks, ramps and ballast tanks on an island ferry during its winter lay-over, so the mainland yard can plan steel renewal before the ship arrives.
Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping survey on a cruise ship that turns round at Palma every week, repeated across visits to trend wall loss.
Hull and tank gauging on a classed superyacht during a refit, covering bottom shell, ballast tanks and engine-room structure once coatings are removed.
Pre-purchase condition gauging of a coaster or ro-ro cargo ship at anchor in the bay, limited to spaces the crew can make safe for entry.
Magnetic particle testing at stabiliser fins, ramp hinges and similar high-load details on a ferry after a bout of heavy weather.

logistics: Palma de Mallorca Airport is close to the harbour and is linked to the main European hubs, so the technicians usually fly in from India through a Gulf or continental connection and reach the quay by road. Spain is part of the Schengen area, and Schengen visas have to be in hand before dates are fixed, so an early enquiry helps. Berth and terminal access, ISPS passes and launch bookings for the bay are arranged through the ship's agent, and yard access is agreed with the refit yard directly.

faqs.q: When is the best season to book gauging in Palma?
faqs.a: Between the end of the summer peak and the start of the next season. Ferries and cruise ships are scheduled tightly from spring to autumn, while winter leaves gaps for docking and survey work. We suggest sending the planned dates as soon as they are fixed so that Schengen visas and travel can be organised.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ferry afloat before it goes to a yard on the mainland?
faqs.a: Yes. Afloat gauging in Palma is a standard way to size steel work. We measure vehicle decks, ramps, stern doors and the tanks the crew can open, then give the owner and the chosen yard a plan of areas near the limits, so the docking scope is realistic before the ship sails.

faqs.q: Do you work on classed superyachts as well as merchant ships?
faqs.a: We gauge large classed yachts with the same ultrasonic method as merchant ships, covering shell, tanks and structure. The brief is agreed with the owner or captain and the attending surveyor, including which areas will be accessible once coatings have been removed and which tanks can be made safe for entry.

faqs.q: Can a cruise ship be gauged during a turnaround day?
faqs.a: Targeted work usually fits. Scrubber piping, sea-water lines and technical voids can be measured while passengers are ashore and the engine department makes space available. A full survey programme will not fit one day, so for larger scopes we spread the readings across several visits and produce a single report.

faqs.q: Does swell in the Bay of Palma stop anchorage work?
faqs.a: It can. A strong southerly swell makes launch boarding uncomfortable and sometimes impossible, so anchorage jobs carry a spare day in the plan. If the ship is going to berth soon, moving the gauging alongside is often the more reliable route.
